**Indikator 12** is a clinical quality indicator used in the Danish healthcare system to monitor the safety and outcomes of treatments for patients with [[atrieflimren]]. Primarily, it is defined as measuring the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who develop severe bleeding within one year, serving as a central quality metric for the safety of anticoagulant therapy [^src1]. However, documentation from the subsequent year indicates a shift or discrepancy in its definition, with the 2024 annual report describing Indikator 12 as measuring the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who die within one year [^src2]. 

In the national reporting for the period of July 1, 2021, to June 30, 2022, the overall proportion of newly diagnosed patients in [[danmark|Danmark]] who suffered severe bleeding within one year was 3.1% (95% CI: 2.8–3.3) [^src1]. The data also highlights variations in patient outcomes at the institutional level. For instance, [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] recorded a severe bleeding rate of 6.0% (95% CI: 3.0–10.5) [^src1], while [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] reported a rate of 4.6% (95% CI: 3.3–6.1) [^src1]. 

The indicator remains a focal point for systematic quality monitoring and benchmarking across regions and hospitals. For the subsequent tracking period from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, Indikator 12 is noted as the active metric for assessing 1-year mortality among newly diagnosed patients, reflecting the updated or alternate definition seen in the 2024 report [^src2].
